name: Barbados
summary_text: Barbados demands real caution. Courts struck down the buggery laws in 2022; Barbados has an organised community (Equals, B-GLAD) and a functioning state. No LGR; modest social conservatism; tourist areas accustomed to diverse visitors.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust page documents Eastern Caribbean constitutional challenges; Barbados decriminalised same-sex conduct in December 2022 via such a constitutional challenge.

sources.title: Antigua and Barbuda: High Court Decriminalizes Gay Sex | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This HRW article is about Antigua and Barbuda's 2022 ruling, not Barbados specifically; included as Eastern Caribbean regional context (Barbados's own High Court struck down its buggery and indecency laws the same year).

sources.title: Barbados: A brush with death, a vigil for trans murder victims
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (Nov 2018): first-person account by Barbadian trans activist Alexa Hoffmann - the country's first Transgender Day of Remembrance vigil; rising trans murder rates globally (369 reported in 2018); her own brush with death; notes 62% of trans murder victims are sex workers and misgendering of victims as 'cross-dressers'.

sources.title: Barbados: No jail time for violent attack on trans activist
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (April 2019): the man who attacked Alexa Hoffmann with a meat cleaver (Feb 2018, serious injuries including to her throat) was ordered to pay BD$460 (~US$230) or serve three months - effectively no jail time; Hoffmann led Barbados's first Pride (2017) and is lead claimant in the challenge to the anti-sodomy law (life imprisonment, 'worst in the Western Hemisphere').

sources.title: Barbados tells bosses it's OK to fire trans workers without cause
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes commentary (Aug 2020) by Alexa Hoffmann: Barbados's Employment (Protection from Discrimination) Bill 2020 omitted gender identity - trans people are frequently denied or fired from jobs for 'dressing wrong'; Hoffmann herself was terminated by a law firm after legally changing her name; the 'Welcome Stamp' remote-worker visa is tainted by discriminatory laws.

sources.title: LGBT activists file challenge of Barbados’ anti-gay laws | Xtra Magazine
sources.claim_summary: Daily Xtra (June 2018): Barbadian activists (Alexa Hoffmann as trans woman claimant, with Canadian support) filed the first challenge to Barbados's Sexual Offences Act at the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights - the law puts trans people in legal jeopardy and enables prejudice and violence.
